submission.name: Bench Breaker
submission.tagline: A little desk-side accountability for campus makers finishing a work session.
submission.inspiration: In a shared workshop, it is easy to wander from a build task into checking a phone, especially when a deadline is close. We wanted a physical reminder that could make a short work block feel more engaging without needing someone else to keep watch.
submission.what_it_does: A webcam checks for phone use during a timed work session, and Gemini confirms likely distractions before generating a short spoken nudge through ElevenLabs. An Arduino controls a small indicator and a brief air puff toward a desk target, giving the reminder a physical cue; Databricks records session events for a simple view of when interruptions happen.
submission.how_we_built_it: A Python and OpenCV loop runs YOLOv8 phone detection on a laptop and sends likely events to Gemini for a quick confirmation and message. ElevenLabs turns that text into audio, while the laptop sends a signal to an Arduino relay that powers a small pump; session events are written to a Databricks table so we can inspect patterns afterward.
submission.challenges_we_ran_into: The camera, model calls, audio playback, Arduino control, and event logging each worked, but keeping them coordinated without delays took most of our time. The detection can mistake a phone-shaped object for a phone, and network lag sometimes makes the spoken cue arrive after the moment has passed; the air puff is also intentionally small and aimed only at a test target.
submission.accomplishments: We connected a live vision loop to both spoken feedback and a physical response, and got the session log flowing into Databricks. We are proud that the project feels tangible at a desk rather than being only another timer window.
submission.what_we_learned: We learned how much timing and hardware safety matter when software triggers a physical device, and why audio should not interrupt the user's work unpredictably. ElevenLabs made the feedback feel more expressive, Gemini helped vary the wording, and Databricks gave us a first look at turning session events into a useful summary.
submission.whats_next: We would like to add user-controlled sensitivity, quieter notification options, and better handling for different desk layouts. We also want to make the event summaries clearer and let users review or delete their session history.
